name: silgy
listed_description: Asynchronous HTTP(S) engine for C/C++ projects. MIT.
reason: Repo README is a three-line deprecation notice pointing to Node++ (rekmus/nodepp); repo page shows no benchmark, req/s or comparison anywhere (79 stars, MIT, deprecated). One WebSearch for Silgy benchmarks found nothing. No numeric comparison against nginx or any other HTTP server.

name: SNMP++
listed_description: A C++ API which supports SNMP v1/2c/v3. License: custom permissive.
reason: agentpp.com is egress-blocked here, so the project page was not opened. WebSearch found no SNMP++ performance claim; DataDog/snmpbench (opened) benchmarks only pysnmp, net-snmp via python3-netsnmp and gosnmp, and does not include SNMP++. It is a protocol API library with no speed claim found. No numbers against any SNMP library.

name: socket99
listed_description: C99 wrapper for the BSD sockets API. ISC.
reason: README (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) is about API ergonomics (one call instead of getaddrinfo/socket/connect/bind/listen); no performance claim of any kind, no benchmark. 146 stars, ISC.

name: tlse
listed_description: Single C file TLS 1.2/1.3 implementation, using tomcrypt as crypto library. BSD-2-Clause.
reason: README and repo page (686 stars, public domain/BSD/MIT) make no performance claim and carry no benchmark; the selling points are single-file size, context export/import for pre-forked workers, KTLS and WebRTC support. Issue search for benchmark/performance/openssl returned only API-behaviour issues (e.g. #69 SSL_read behaviour), no numbers. One WebSearch found no third-party tlse vs OpenSSL measurement. No numeric comparison against OpenSSL.

name: TreeFrog Framework
listed_description: High-speed and full-stack web application framework based on C++ and Qt, which supports HTTP and WebSocket protocol (with O/R mapping). BSD.
reason: Directional claim only in what could be opened: README says applications 'can run faster than that of lightweight programming language' with no numbers; docs/en/user-guide/performance/index.md has one 2010 httperf run (TreeFrog 0.54, Qt 4.7, Core 2 Duo, 561.8 req/s on blogapp, no external baseline) and an internal comparison (thread MPM about 14x of the deprecated prefork MPM), neither against a recognizable baseline. The project's blog (docs/en/blog/index.md, docs/ja/blog/index.md) points to TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks rounds 9, 13 and 22 and the Japanese post says it was 'in the top group among MVC frameworks' in round 9 (no numbers). The TFB result pages (techempower.com) and cutelyst.org's round-13 write-up are egress-blocked here; a WebSearch snippet (not opened) said round 13 had treefrog-thread at 312,573 rps (4.6% of the top entry) and treefrog (MySQL) at 17,545 rps (0.3% of the top), i.e. far behind the leaders, not a win over a named baseline. Lead: TFB per-round data for treefrog vs Rails/Django/Spring rows if a session can reach techempower.com; frameworks/C++/treefrog in TechEmpower/FrameworkBenchmarks was archived 2026-03-24 per its page.

name: Tufão
listed_description: An asynchronous web framework for C++ built on top of Qt. LGPL2.
reason: README says only 'High performance standalone server' (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com page; 595 stars, maintainer says can no longer maintain it); no numbers, no benchmark, no comparison. One WebSearch for Tufão benchmarks found only Cutelyst TFB posts that do not mention Tufão. Directional claim without numbers, project not notable enough for a tier D record.

name: twitc
listed_description: Mini library for interacting with the Twitter OAuth API. MIT.
reason: README (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) describes a liboauth + json-c Twitter API client; no performance claim or benchmark. Not an HTTP server; the guessed category and baseline were wrong.
